sentence: This project builds a pipeline that sequences samples and produces gene expression data sets to study vaccine response in rhesus macaque.
This project combines several data sets to find biological signatures of addiction and HIV in the brains of non-human models.
This project uses existing cohort study data to test whether blood fatty acid patterns can predict age-related macular degeneration or glaucoma.
This project studies how recombinant poliovirus stimulates antigen presenting cells to help the immune system attack tumors.
This project builds tools and data sets for studying natural variation in three Caenorhabditis species, including resistance to toxicants and drugs.
This project studies how radiation therapy affects sarcoma and normal tissue in mice, human cell lines and patient samples, alone and with immunotherapy.
This project studies how networks of cells and molecules cause lasting respiratory problems after infection, and explores possible treatments.
This project studies the brain connections from the parabigeminal region to the dorsal lateral geniculate nucleus in mice that support visual motion perception.
This project provides statistical and computer support for sarcoma research, including designing clinical trials and analyzing data.
This project develops molecules that block how DEAD-box helicases bind RNA, using bifunctional molecules and molecular glues.
This project studies how oxidation of a copper uptake transporter in endothelial cells affects inflammation and programmed cell death in atherosclerosis.
This project studies how exposure to many chemicals, including those in personal care products, affects ovarian health and female fertility.
This project supports brain research on the healthy brain and neural disorders, and on the neural basis of behavior and cognition.
This project tracks behavior and clinical markers in people going through mental health treatment to build tools that match patients to treatments.
This project builds AI methods that add up radiation dose in abdominal organs, and tests them with virtual digital twins.
This project studies how mild traumatic brain injury changes the lateral habenula and leads to lasting problems in motivated behaviors in mice.
This project uses CRISPR base editing to test how genetic variants change the risk of heart and blood diseases.
This project studies how memory B cells stay in the lungs and keep up the chronic allergic response in allergic asthma.
This project builds computer and statistical methods to study how human genetic variation shapes genome function and evolution using DNA sequence data.
This project engineers peptide-based nanoparticles that deliver genome editing agents to targeted cell populations in vivo.
